exposure: Increased white blood cell (WBC) in blood test
cohort: The study included 134 asymptomatic women with singleton pregnancies diagnosed with cervical shortening (<=25 mm) during routine universal screening at 22-33 weeks.
finding: Uterine contractions (aOR 4.25) and elevated C-reactive protein (aOR 3.45) were identified as significant additional risk factors for preterm delivery among women with a short cervix.
gest_age: Cervical shortening was detected at 22-33 weeks of gestation.
